CheckTitle: Ensure users with administrative access through group membership have MFA enabled
Description: IAM users who are members of groups granting administrative access must have MFA enabled. This is a composite check derived from CIS 1.10 (MFA for console users) applied specifically to the subset of users identified by CIS 1.16 criteria (administrative access). It is not itself a numbered CIS control. Administrative access without MFA represents the combination of maximum privilege with a single-factor authentication barrier.
Risk: An administrative user without MFA requires only a compromised password for full account control. This is the highest-risk credential configuration for non-root principals — maximum privilege with minimum authentication assurance.
Remediation: Enable MFA for all users in groups with administrative policies (CIS 1.10). Enforce MFA via IAM policy condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent on the group or role trust policy.
SeverityBasis: Composite of CIS AWS 3.0.0 Control 1.10 (MFA for console users, Level 1) and Control 1.16 (no admin privileges, Level 1). This check is not independently enumerated in CIS; it applies CIS 1.10 to the high-risk subset defined by CIS 1.16 criteria. High severity reflects that the combination of maximum privilege and absent MFA is the highest-risk non-root credential state.
AuthoritativeSource: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: CIS AWS 3.0.0 - 1.10 (Level 1) applied to principals meeting 1.16 (Level 1) criteria; composite check, not an individually numbered CIS control
